itinerary.cal: The Middle Fork Nooksack bridge/log crossing at the start of the Elbow Lake Trail washes out periodically - check recent trip reports before relying on a dry crossing.

days.note: Fit parties often do this as one long car-to-car day; others camp in the Green Creek basin. While FS Road 38 is closed by its washout, biking the closed road miles saves the legs. From the trailhead, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack, hike the Elbow Lake Trail through old growth to the Hildebrand Creek switchback, and follow the blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' trail into the cirque, across the low-angle glacier to the Cinderella-Little Sister notch and up the west ridge on grippy olivine rock to the summit. Descend by reversing the route, including re-biking the closed road miles at the end.
days.title: Bike/hike approach and ridge scramble to the summit

schedule.label: Leave car, bike the logging road
schedule.detail: FS Road 38 is closed by a washout at milepost 7, about 4 miles short of the trailhead; biking those closed miles saves time and legs.

schedule.label: Stash bikes, start Elbow Lake Trail on foot
schedule.detail: Cross the Middle Fork Nooksack right at the trailhead (no bridge), then climb through old growth above the Green Creek valley about 1.5 mi to the Hildebrand Creek switchback, where the blue-blazed Green Creek climbers' trail branches off.

schedule.label: Reach the Green Creek cirque
schedule.detail: Talus, loose scree and Class 3 rock steps lead to the toe of the glacier; cross it to the notch between Cinderella and Little Sister.

schedule.label: Ridge/gully scramble to Cinderella summit
schedule.detail: Class 3-4 scrambling on solid, high-friction olivine rock; some exposed ridge sections and route-finding around gendarmes.

schedule.label: Reverse the scramble and hike back to bikes
schedule.detail: Downclimb the ridge, retrace the glacier, the Green Creek climbers' trail and the Elbow Lake Trail.

schedule.label: Bike out to the car
schedule.detail: Mostly downhill/flat closed-road miles back to the vehicle.

days.objective: Summit Cinderella Peak via the west ridge olivine scramble, car-to-car

itinerary.totalNote: A long single push: roughly 11-12 hours car-to-car, ~12 miles and ~5,400 ft of gain, done in a day, as many fit parties do.

road.name: Forest Road 38 (Mosquito Lake Road to Elbow Lake Trailhead)
road.status: Closed at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026 — this blocks vehicle access to the Elbow Lake Trailhead, which is about 11 miles in. Good gravel and paved forest road when open; check the forest's alerts page before driving.
road.driveNote: From Mosquito Lake Road near Deming/Acme, turn east onto FS Road 38 and drive about 11 miles of forest road to the Elbow Lake Trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Gated at Wallace Creek, about 1.3 miles before the trailhead, roughly Dec 1-Jun 15.

itinerary.cal: Best done once the brushy approach and ridge are fully snow-free, typically mid-summer through early fall (roughly July-September).

days.note: This is a big single-day outing, not a backpack: parties hike the Elbow Lake Trail, ford the Middle Fork Nooksack and follow the blazed Green Creek climbers' path into the Green Creek Cirque, then scramble loose third and fourth class ground out of the cirque onto the ridge where the terrain turns to famously grippy olivine/dunite rock. Skookum's north ridge is reached by going over Jaws' Tooth and rappelling (or downclimbing low fifth class) to the notch on its south side; from there the line stays true to the crest on solid, very exposed rock at about 5.4. The way down is the loose south-west side by third-class gullies, not back along the ridge.
days.title: Car-to-car: Elbow Lake Trail and Green Creek Cirque + Skookum north ridge

schedule.label: Leave the trailhead
schedule.detail: Start hiking in the dark to bank time; the Middle Fork Nooksack ford comes within the first quarter mile.

schedule.label: Leave the trail for the Green Creek path
schedule.detail: At a switchback near Hildebrand Creek the blazed climbers' path leaves the maintained trail and heads into the Green Creek Cirque.

schedule.label: Gain the ridge crest
schedule.detail: Forest opens onto exposed olivine/dunite rock; follow the crest to Jaws' Tooth and rappel or downclimb to the notch below Skookum.

schedule.label: Climb the north ridge to the summit
schedule.detail: Roped, exposed 5.4 climbing on the crest; most parties top out by late morning to early afternoon.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Descend the loose south-west side by third-class gullies rather than reversing the ridge; watch for rockfall.

schedule.label: Back at the car
schedule.detail: Retrace the Green Creek path and the Elbow Lake Trail, fording the Middle Fork again on the way out.

days.objective: Summit Skookum Peak via the Elbow Lake Trail, the Green Creek Cirque and the olivine (dunite) ridge

itinerary.totalNote: A long but standard single day: roughly 9-11 hours car-to-car, ~14 miles round trip and ~4,200 ft of gain, mixing a long trail and climbers'-path approach with a roped 5.4 ridge on grippy olivine rock.

road.name: Forest Road 38 (via Mosquito Lake Road from Acme) to the Elbow Lake Trail's north trailhead (a separate trailhead from Pioneer Camp, which is on the trail's south end via Baker Lake Highway/FSR 12)
road.status: Closed to vehicles at a flood washout near milepost 7 — confirm current status with the Mount Baker Ranger District before driving in.
road.driveNote: From the Mount Baker Ranger District (Sedro-Woolley), take WA-9 north to Acme, turn right on Mosquito Lake Road for ~9 miles, cross the Middle Fork Nooksack River, then continue on FSR 38 for ~11 miles to the trailhead.
road.seasonalGate: Normally gated at Wallace Creek (~1.3 miles before the trailhead) roughly December 1 through June 15, independent of flood damage.

itinerary.cal: Best window is a narrow spring stretch (roughly April-June) when overnight refreeze holds the couloir's snow/ice/rock together; too early risks fresh-snow avalanche, too late risks wet-slide and rockfall on the crumbling volcanic rock.

days.note: Drive FR-38 to around the mile-12.5 switchback, then hike/bushwhack the old decommissioned road around Pt. 4481 toward Rankin Creek. Snow travel (often bike or snowshoes on the lower stretch) leads past East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft) and up into the basin to a sheltered camp at treeline.
days.title: Approach to basin camp

schedule.label: Leave trailhead / switchback
schedule.detail: Bike or hike the closed FR-38 switchbacks as snow cover allows.

schedule.label: Bushwhack past Pt. 4481
schedule.detail: Follow the old road around the point's slopes toward Rankin Creek through alder.

schedule.label: Reach East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft)
schedule.detail: Switch to snowshoes; continue north through snow slopes to a saddle.

schedule.label: Make camp at 6,100 ft
schedule.detail: Sheltered site near the highest trees in the basin below Seward Peak.

days.objective: Reach the ~6,100 ft camp near Rankin Creek/Rankin Lake basin

days.note: An alpine start gets the team into the SW basin and across the bergschrund crux while it's still cold and firm, up ~1,500 ft of 30-40° snow and a steep serac step to the summit. Descent reverses the route with roughly ten double-rope rappels off pickets and rock-horn anchors, then camp is broken and the party hikes out the same evening.
days.title: Summit day: X Couloir

schedule.label: Wake at camp
schedule.detail: Brew up and gear up for the alpine start.

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Head up into the SW basin toward the bergschrund.

schedule.label: Cross the bergschrund
schedule.detail: Crux step (AI3+/steep serac); weave through gaps rather than bridging.

schedule.label: Summit (9,085 ft)
schedule.detail: Roughly 5 hours from camp via the X Couloir.

schedule.label: Rappel the couloir
schedule.detail: About ten double-rope (2x60m) rappels off pickets and rock horns back to camp.

schedule.label: Hike out to trailhead
schedule.detail: Break camp and retrace the approach to the vehicle.

days.objective: Climb the SW basin / bergschrund / X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit and return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip: ~7 mi and 3,350 ft up to a 6,100 ft basin camp on day 1, then a 1:45-3 AM alpine start, bergschrund crux, and X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit on day 2, descending via roughly ten rappels back to camp and hiking out the same evening.

road.name: Forest Road 38 (Middle Fork Nooksack / Wallace Creek Road)
road.status: First ~2 miles passable by passenger car; remaining ~10.5 miles to the mile-12.5 switchback are rough, potholed, and brushy — high-clearance/4WD recommended.
road.driveNote: Road condition and washout status can change year to year; call the Glacier Public Service Center for current beta before driving.
road.seasonalGate: Reported gated at Wallace Creek (about 1.3 miles before a nearby trailhead) roughly Dec 1-Jun 15 in some seasons to protect elk breeding habitat; exact Road 38 gate point varies by year

road.name: Middle Fork Nooksack River Rd / FR 12 & FR 38 to Elbow Lake Trailhead
road.status: Closed at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert still posted on 25 September 2026 — this blocks vehicle access to the Elbow Lake Trailhead.
road.driveNote: Unpaved logging roads near active/former timber and Olivine Corp land; drive respectfully.
road.seasonalGate: FR 12 closed to vehicles from Rocky Creek Bridge (MP 4.6) for road repairs from late August through 1 October 2026, as listed on the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert; FR 38 washout/barrier at MP 7.

road.name: Forest Road 38 (Middle Fork Nooksack Road)
road.status: Closed at milepost 7 due to a washout, per a Mt Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest alert dated 27 July 2026 — this blocks vehicle access to the Elbow Lake Trail 697 north trailhead and to Ridley Creek Trail 696. Verify current status on the forest's alerts page before driving. Separately, FR 12 (the southern approach to the Elbow Lake Trail via Pioneer Camp) was scheduled closed from Rocky Creek Bridge at MP 4.6 between 10-24 August 2026 for road repairs, remaining open to foot, bike and e-bike.
road.driveNote: From the Mt. Baker Ranger District office in Sedro-Woolley, drive north on Highway 9 to Acme. About 7.2-7.6 miles past the office, after crossing the South Fork Nooksack River, turn right on Mosquito Lake Road and follow it roughly 9 miles. After crossing the Middle Fork Nooksack River, turn right onto Forest Road 38 and drive about 11-12 miles to the Elbow Lake Trailhead on the right, with parking directly across the road. FR 38 is dirt and subject to washouts. Coming from Bellingham, reach Mosquito Lake Road via Highway 542 through Deming. Note that despite the 'Mt Baker Hwy' area label, SR 542 is not the access road for this peak.
road.seasonalGate: FR 38 is gated at Wallace Creek, 1.3 miles below the trailhead. Forest Service trail pages list the gate closure as Dec 1 - Jun 15; other Forest Service pages give Nov 1 - Jun 15. The southern access, FR 12, is gated Nov 1 - Jun 30 at Wanlick Pass.
